rows.selection_reason: No experiments have been completed, so the main uncertainty is whether a simple RNA-only representation provides a useful performance baseline before adding multiprofile aggregation, learned encoders, image features, or fusion. config_001 tests the simplest RNA-only single-profile PCA model, isolating the effect of basic RNA representation without confounding changes to profile setting, aggregation, or fusion. It is the best first use of a limited budget because it is low-complexity, cheap to interpret, and establishes an anchor for later comparisons against multiprofile, alternative RNA encoders, image-only, and multimodal configurations.

The only completed experiment is an RNA-only single-profile PCA baseline with modest accuracy (0.485) and F1 (0.464), so it is still unclear whether the image modality contains useful predictive signal. config_010 tests the simplest image-only baseline using a standard ResNet50 and single-profile input, which establishes a unimodal image reference without introducing aggregation or fusion complexity. This is the best next experiment under a limited budget because it directly reduces uncertainty about the value of the image modality before investing in more complex multimodal or multiprofile configurations, and it is directly comparable to later multimodal ResNet50 settings.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only PCA singleprofile substantially outperforms image-only ResNet singleprofile, so RNA is the stronger modality, but it is unclear whether multiprofile aggregation improves RNA performance. config_002 tests this by keeping the same RNA encoder and modality while moving to multiprofile with the simplest avgpool aggregation, isolating the profile/aggregation effect as much as possible. It is the best next experiment because it exploits the promising RNA direction with a minimal change; if it helps, it justifies testing transformer aggregation or multimodal multiprofile extensions, and if it does not, it indicates singleprofile may be sufficient before adding complexity.

RNA-only multiprofile with PCA and avgpool is currently the strongest result, showing that multiprofile aggregation substantially improves over single-profile RNA. Image-only is weak, so the main open question is whether a stronger aggregation method can further improve the promising RNA multiprofile setting. config_003 tests transformer aggregation while keeping the model, profile setting, and RNA encoder fixed, isolating the effect of aggregation. This is the best next use of budget because it extends the current best direction and reduces uncertainty about a key design choice before moving to more complex multimodal models.

The strongest evidence so far is RNA-only PCA with multiprofile avgpool (0.591 acc / 0.573 F1), while image-only ResNet with singleprofile is weak (0.208 acc / 0.172 F1). It is unclear whether the image modality can contribute at all or whether the multiprofile avgpool benefit seen in RNA is general. config_011 tests image-only ResNet with multiprofile avgpool, directly extending config_010 and mirroring the profile/aggregation setting of the best RNA result. This is the best next experiment because it isolates the effect of profile setting and aggregation for the image modality, reducing uncertainty about whether multimodal or image-based extensions are worth further budget.

Completed experiments show that RNA PCA with multiprofile avgpool is the current best setting (0.591 accuracy, 0.573 F1), and avgpool multiprofile also improves image ResNet, so profile aggregation is a proven lever. The key uncertainty is whether a learned RNA representation improves over PCA under this same promising setting. config_005 tests scVI_n200 while keeping multiprofile avgpool fixed, isolating the RNA encoder effect. This is the best next use of budget because it is a one-factor extension of the current best, may raise the unimodal baseline before adding multimodal complexity, and will clarify whether representation learning is an important design choice for future multimodal models.

The strongest evidence so far is RNA-only multiprofile with avgpool, where scvi_n200 outperforms pca_n200 (0.650 vs 0.591 accuracy) and avgpool outperforms transformer for pca. The main remaining uncertainty among unimodal RNA designs is whether scgpt can match or exceed scvi under the same profile and aggregation setting. config_008 tests this cleanly by changing only the RNA encoder while keeping multiprofile and avgpool fixed. This is a good use of the next experiment because it identifies the best RNA representation before spending budget on more complex multimodal or fusion variants.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile avgpool helps both RNA and image, but image-only ResNet remains much weaker than RNA (0.328 vs 0.650), and ViT image representation is untested. config_014 tests whether a stronger image encoder improves image-only accuracy under the same multiprofile avgpool setting as config_011, isolating image representation. This is the best next experiment because it is a one-factor comparison, balances exploration of the image modality with exploitation of the preferred profile/aggregation, and clarifies whether image features are worth adding in multimodal fusion before spending budget on more complex fusion configurations.

The strongest evidence so far is RNA-only multiprofile with scvi_n200 and avgpool (config_005: 0.6501 acc, 0.6275 F1), while image-only models remain weak (about 0.21-0.33 acc). The key unresolved question is whether adding image features to the best RNA setting provides any complementary signal. config_030 tests this by extending config_005 with a tested image encoder (resnet50) and the simplest fusion baseline (concat), while keeping the RNA encoder, profile setting, and aggregation fixed at their best-performing values. This is the most informative next experiment because it directly evaluates the value of multimodality under the current best representation; if it improves, it justifies further fusion/image-encoder exploration, and if it does not, it discourages spending budget on more complex multimodal variants.

RNA-only scvi_n200 with multiprofile avgpool is currently the best single-modality result (0.6501 acc, 0.6275 F1), while the closest multimodal test, scvi_n200 + resnet50 with avgpool and concat fusion, is slightly lower (0.6315 acc, 0.6068 F1). The main uncertainty is whether the small multimodal gap is due to the image modality being weak or to the simple concat fusion being suboptimal. config_031 changes only the fusion method from concat to weighted while keeping the strongest RNA encoder, image encoder, profile setting, and aggregation fixed. This is a focused, low-risk extension of the best multimodal evidence and will clarify whether weighted fusion can make the multimodal model competitive with the RNA-only baseline before investing further in more complex multimodal variants.
